key_insight: Trainability in adaptive variational quantum chemistry can be trapped by the fermion-to-qubit representation itself, so point-group symmetry alone does not guarantee an easy optimization landscape.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum algorithm design, the qubit mapping, molecular symmetry, and adaptive measurement strategy must be co-designed to avoid representation-induced flat regions and wasted circuit depth.
method: Evaluated a spin-conserved SUSD operator pool on stretched LiH, BeH2, and H2O geometries.
Compared asymmetric distortions against the symmetric BeH2 baseline to isolate symmetry-protection effects.
Added a covariance-driven adaptive shot-allocation filter that monitors gradient precision and terminates when the optimization becomes flat.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation across highly stretched configurations at 2×Re and identifies optimization trapping under asymmetric geometries with Bravyi-Kitaev mapping, while symmetric BeH2 remains structurally protected.
watch_item: The runtime pruning and circuit-termination logic may be sensitive to threshold choice and could prematurely stop useful exploration in noisy, near-flat regions.
paper_title: Representation-Induced Symmetry Trapping in Adaptive Variational Quantum Simulations of Multi-Reference Topologies
